tree.label: Linguistics & Computer Science BA — Major Requirements

children.label: Grade minimum
children.note: All 15 courses need a C or better. This isn't checked automatically.
children.devNote: Bulletin: 15 courses 'all completed with a grade of C or higher'. minGrade is set at the top level but the engine doesn't check grades. Honors in the Major is not modeled.

children.label: Calculus
children.note: Calculus at about the level of MA 123 is expected for this major. It isn't one of the 15 courses and isn't checked automatically.
children.devNote: Bulletin: students 'are also expected to be comfortable with standard high school mathematics as well as calculus at a level equivalent to completion of CAS MA 123.' Not one of the 15 courses.

children.label: Linguistics: required courses
children.devNote: Bulletin: 'Six courses in Linguistics' = LX 250, 301, 321, 331 + two additional LX courses at or above the 300 level (separate node below). Fixed courses are evaluated first so the broad LX ranges later can't claim them.

children.label: Linguistics: two additional courses (LX 300 or above)
children.devNote: Bulletin: 'Two additional CAS LX courses at or above the 300 level', listed right after the four required LX courses. It is a REMAINDER (totalRequired 15 = the 13 other courses + these 2) so it evaluates last, after the Computational Linguistics/NLP and additional-course nodes, and can't take LX 496 or an LX 400-level course they need. LX 301/321/331 and any LX course already used elsewhere are claimed earlier and not counted twice. If a sibling's size changes, recompute totalRequired.
children.note: Any LX course numbered 300 or above that isn't already counting somewhere else in this major.

children.label: Computer Science: required courses
children.devNote: Bulletin: 'Seven courses in Computer Science'. Unlike the CS BA, this bulletin lists no MA substitutes for CS 132 or CS 237, so none are modeled.

children.label: Computational Linguistics or NLP (1)
children.devNote: Bulletin: one course from CS 505 or LX 496. CS 505 is listed first so a student with both keeps LX 496 free for the 'additional course' node (LX 496 is a 400-level LX course). This node is listed before the additional-course node, unlike the bulletin, so it claims first: the additional course's LX 400-499 range would otherwise take a lone LX 496.
children.note: LX 496 and CS 505 both count here. If you take both, one counts here and the other can count as your additional course.

children.label: One additional course: CS 542 or an LX 400-level course
children.devNote: Bulletin: 'One additional course in Computer Science or Linguistics': CS 542, or one LX course at the 400 level. CS 542 first, then the LX 400-499 range. Study-abroad (E-suffixed) keys are skipped by range matching on purpose. Evaluated before the two additional LX 300+ courses so a 400-level course fills this slot first.
children.note: LX 496 can count here too, but not if it's already counting as your Computational Linguistics/NLP course.
